extracted.intended_audience: comic/cartoon creators, students of comics, graphic-novel writers/artists, and readers studying comics craft
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles and topic-by-topic criteria for creating comics, manga, and graphic novels (story, character, image/word integration, worldbuilding, and tools) as organized in Scott McCloud's Making Comics. Useful for practitioners learning craft and instructors developing exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and Persuasion
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed as a primary topic in the 'Writing with Pictures' section — addresses how comics communicate ideas clearly while persuading the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: McCloud illustrates principles with historical examples; complex topics are often reduced to a few actionable principles. No detailed scoring provided on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Five Choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Named topic in 'Writing with Pictures' — a framework McCloud uses for decisions creators make when composing comics (implied as five fundamental choices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book reportedly breaks down major compositional choices; Wikipedia notes McCloud often reduces complex topics to a few principles and provides examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of Moment
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic under 'Writing with Pictures' emphasizing choosing the exact moment to depict in a panel or sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of compositional decision-making that affects narrative clarity and emotional impact; examples and exercises appear in the book (per page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of Frame
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic under 'Writing with Pictures' focused on selecting panel boundaries and framing to control reader focus and pacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing is presented alongside other 'choices' that shape clarity, flow, and persuasion; book contains examples and exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of Image
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'Writing with Pictures' concerning what to show visually to tell the story effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that images must be selected to serve clarity and persuasion; examples drawn from comics history illustrate tradeoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of Word
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'Writing with Pictures' about selecting words (dialogue, captions) to pair with images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of McCloud's integrated approach to image+word; book covers word-picture relationships and gives practical guidance and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of Flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'Writing with Pictures' addressing the sequencing and directional flow of panels to guide reader movement through the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flow interacts with frame and moment choices to shape readability and narrative pacing; exercises and notes conclude the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'Writing with Pictures' covering approaches to working as a comics creator (workflow, process-level choices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes practical tips on methods McCloud used (e.g., digital drawing on a tablet); page notes that the first four sections end with notes and exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity vs. Intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'Writing with Pictures' about balancing clear communication with intense, emotionally charged presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: McCloud contrasts clarity and intensity as tradeoffs creators manage; illustrated with examples, but no numeric scoring on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intensity vs. Persuasion
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'Writing with Pictures' addressing the relationship between the intensity of presentation and the persuasive power of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positioned alongside other tradeoff topics; examples and principles in the book show how to balance these aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetry and Recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic listed in the 'Stories for Humans' section — concerns visual or narrative symmetry and how recognition principles help readers understand characters and story beats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tied to creating stories that resonate with human perception and pattern recognition; book gives examples from comics history.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3 Steps to Believable Characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'Stories for Humans' outlining a three-step process McCloud recommends for making characters believable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescriptive mini-framework for character believability; the Wikipedia page lists the topic but does not reproduce the steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Design
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'Stories for Humans' focusing on how to design characters visually and narratively to serve story needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses visual traits, symbolic choices, and recognition; illustrated with examples and exercises in the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facial Expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'Stories for Humans' about using faces to convey emotion and intention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linked to McCloud's discussion of 'six basic emotions' and the ways simplified cartooning can clearly communicate affect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body Language
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'Stories for Humans' covering how posture and gesture communicate character and subtext.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a component of believable character work along with facial expression and design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance and Integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'The Power of Words' section concerning how words and pictures balance and integrate to tell the story effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leads into McCloud's taxonomy of word/picture relationships and practical advice for integrating text and image.

rubrics_metrics.name: The 7 Types of Word/Picture Combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit topic in 'The Power of Words' — McCloud's taxonomy categorizing how words and pictures can relate (seven types).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core conceptual rubric for evaluating or designing how text and image interact; Wikipedia notes the topic title but not the seven types themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word Balloons
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'The Power of Words' about the design and use of speech/word balloons in comics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers form, placement, and readability considerations for balloons; part of broader word-picture integration guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'The Power of Words' addressing onomatopoeia and how SFX are rendered and integrated into panels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines role of sound effects in the visual language of comics and their effect on reader perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writer/Artist Collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'The Power of Words' discussing collaborative processes between writers and artists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers practical considerations for joint creative workflows and division of responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Picking Your Story
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'The Power of Words' about selecting which story to tell (subject matter, scope, and fit for medium).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises creators on matching story choice to strengths and intended readership; paired with 'Heritage and Strengths' guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heritage and Strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'The Power of Words' that encourages creators to recognize their background, influences, and strengths when choosing how to tell stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames story-picking as aligning personal/genre heritage with creative strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Being There
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'World Building' about creating the sense of presence — making readers feel 'there' in a place and time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes discussion of establishing shots and perspective to root readers in setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisiting the Establishing Shot
rubrics_metrics.description: World-building topic that reconsiders how and when to use establishing shots to orient readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of McCloud's practical advice for pacing and scene-setting in sequential art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional Variations
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'World Building' on how setting and cultural/regional detail affect storytelling and design choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages research and attention to local color and differences when building worlds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic Strip Minimalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'World Building' covering minimalist approaches specific to comic strips and brevity-focused formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses constraints-driven design choices and how minimalism can still convey setting and character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'World Building' about using perspective drawing to create believable space and depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical guidance on spatial representation that supports immersion and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference and Research
rubrics_metrics.description: World-building topic stressing the importance of using references and research to inform accurate and convincing settings and details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly encourages creators to use research; the book provides examples and exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not Just Backgrounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'World Building' arguing that backgrounds should do more than fill space — they should support story, character, and theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reframes backgrounds as active storytelling elements rather than passive scenery.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Only Essential Tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic in 'Tools, Techniques, & Technology' identifying which tools McCloud considers essential for comics-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Likely a minimal recommended toolkit; the Wikipedia page lists the topic but not the specific tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing on the Cheap
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic offering low-cost approaches to producing comics (budget techniques and economical materials/workflows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical advice for creators with limited resources; McCloud recounts digital-drawing choices in development notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional Tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic detailing non-digital, traditional art tools for making comics (inks, pens, paper, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers tradeoffs between traditional media and other approaches; examples and equipment notes accompany the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic about digital techniques and tools for creating comics (tablets, software, digital workflows).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page notes McCloud drew the book on a Cintiq; discusses ergonomics and workflow advantages of digital drawing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lettering and Fonts
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic on the design and use of lettering and font choices to affect readability and tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses balloon lettering, type choices, and integration with art; part of the tools/techniques section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic covering physical equipment needed for producing comics (hardware, studio setup, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes mention of digital tablet ergonomics and other practical equipment considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing Alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic outlining different publishing paths for comics (traditional publishing, self-publishing, online).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes McCloud's experience promoting the book (tour) and discussion of publishing options; useful for career/practical planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classifying cartoonists into four types
rubrics_metrics.description: McCloud's noted principle of categorizing cartoonists into four types (mentioned as an example of the book distilling complex topics into a few principles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced as an illustrative simplification technique used in the book; Wikipedia does not list the four types explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: The six basic emotions
rubrics_metrics.description: McCloud's identification of six basic emotions used as an analytical/teaching device (mentioned on the page as an example of topic simplification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a concise rubric for depicting emotion in comics; the page references the concept but does not enumerate the six emotions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section notes and exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement that the first four sections of the book conclude with notes and exercises to practice the material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies an applied/practice-oriented pedagogy: each major topic is followed by exercises to reinforce concepts.
